title.narrative: COVID-19: Emergency Assistance for COVID-19 Pandemic Response

description.narrative: Taking into account the needs of the country and the priorities established by the National Emergency Response Plan for Coronavirus 2020 (NERP), Asian Development Bank's (ADB) emergency assistance covers: rehabilitation and construction of hospitals and medical facilities for the treatment of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) infected patients in most affected areas; procurement of medical equipment, supplies and medicines; and capacity building and resilience strengthening of the national health system to respond to public health emergencies including COVID-19; and related project management and monitoring system support.

Output: Hospitals and medical facilities rehabilitated or constructed Indicator: At least 15 hospitals constructed and equipped with all the essential amenities, such as power generators and waste incinerators, and have dedicated wards for female patients and separate offices and lounge spaces for women doctors and nurses Progress/Status: The contract for construction of phase 1 (ie., 10 hospital facilities) was signed on 2 Sep 2020. The construction works commenced on 18 Oct 2020. Out of 10 hospitals; 3 hospitals at Paktia, Faryab, and and Samangan were completed and accepted by the previous government; 3 hospitals at Sarepol, Zabul, and Badghis were ready for acceptance; and 3 others in Helmand, Dykundi, and Urozgan were more than 90% completed at the time of collapse in August 2021. The construction of hospital in Ghor commenced in July 2021 with little progress made until 15 AUG 2021. Following the government collapse in August 2021, ADB paused its operations in Afghanistan.
The contract award for the additional five hospitals (phase 2) was at the final stage but was delayed due to the arising circumstances in the country. This included hospitals at Ghazni, Nangarhar, Paktika, Noristan and Takhar.
Following the Taliban takeover, all ADB operations in Afghanistan have been put on hold including this emergency assistance effective 15 of August 2021. Data Source: Periodic progress reports prepared by MOPH Actual value:

Output: Hospitals and medical facilities rehabilitated or constructed Indicator: At least five hospitals and medical facilities rehabilitated following the “build back better” principle and include women-friendly and culturally sensitive facilities Progress/Status: This output was not achieved as ADB's operations were paused following the previous government collapse in August 2021. Data Source: Periodic progress reports prepared by MOPH Actual value:

Output: Medicines and medical equipment supplied Indicator: 100% of the female medical staff working in hospitals covered under output 1 are equipped with proper fitting personal protective suits, face shields, masks, and goggles; and menstrual hygiene kits, as needed Progress/Status: The supply and installation of medical equipment and medicine contracts with WHO and UNICEF were signed on 2 Sep 2020. All contracted supplies were delivered.
The contracts for non-medical equipment were signed in early April 2021. The delivery of these items was divided into 2 lots. The equipment under lot 1 were fully delivered before 15 August 2021. The equipment under lot 2 was delayed following the government collapse in Afghanistan.
ADB paused its operations in Afghanistan after August 2021. Data Source: Periodic progress reports prepared by MOPH, WHO, and UNICEF Actual value:
